title: Interview: John Lennon for Rolling Stone | 1980
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono were interviewed by Jonathan Cott for Rolling Stone magazine in the evening of 5 December 1980.

The interview took place at the couple’s Dakota Building home. They discussed subjects including Lennon’s retreat from the public eye and return to recording, his Bermuda vacation, critics’ responses to his music, his son Sean, the making of the Double Fantasy album, and his hopes for the future.

Although the interview was originally scheduled to be the cover story of the first Rolling Stone issue of 1981, it was mostly shelved and replaced by an obituary by Cott. It was finally transcribed and printed in full in 2010 as “John Lennon: The Last Interview”, although Lennon gave three subsequent interviews after 5 December.

Sometimes you wonder, I mean really wonder. I know we make our own reality, and we always have a choice, but how much is preordained? Is there always a fork in the road, and are there two preordained paths that are equally preordained? There could be hundreds of paths where one could go this way or that way – there’s a choice, and it’s very strange sometimes.
John Lennon, 5 December 1980
Rolling Stone

As the interview concluded, Cott accompanied Lennon and Ono to the Hit Factory studio, where preparations were being made for a forthcoming release by Ono. The recording session concluded at 4am the following morning.
